## Confirmed

The scan's three duplication findings hold up against the source. I read all six files; here's what's actually there.

**`near_duplicate_block` (crime_00001) — the real target.** `sanitizeUserInput` (`src/sanitize-a.ts:10-36`), `sanitizeText` (`src/sanitize-b.ts:9-35`), and `cleanMessage` (`src/sanitize-c.ts:9-35`) are token-for-token identical apart from the local variable name (`working` / `cleaned` / `normalised`) and the parameter name (`raw` / `input` / `value`). Same trim, same `replace(/[ -]/g, "")`, same 1000-char cap, same `<`/`>` prefix reject, same `\\x` reject, same `>5` punctuation-run reject, same 0.9 upper-ratio / 30-char shouting fold. There is **no behavioural divergence to preserve** — this is a straight three-into-one extraction, not a parameterised merge. The finding's `fix_shape` ("pass the differing values as args") is more cautious than the code requires.

**`exact_duplicate_block` (crime_00002).** `recordSanitiseEvent` in `telemetry-a.ts:6-19` and `telemetry-b.ts:6-19` are byte-identical, comment header included.

**`duplicated_role_status_plan_check` (crime_00003) — the trap.** The literal `"admin"` appears in four files across *three* real semantics, not two:

| Site | Expression | Means |
|---|---|---|
| `policy.ts:3,8,13` | `role === "admin"` | admin only |
| `sanitize-a.ts:7` (`assertAdminA`) | `role === "admin"` | admin only |
| `sanitize-b.ts:6` (`assertAdminB`) | `role === "admin" \|\| role === "owner"` | admin **or owner** |
| `sanitize-c.ts:6` (`assertAdminC`) | `role !== "admin"` | **inverted** — returns `true` for non-admins |

`assertAdminC` is named like an admin assertion and returns the opposite. Folding all four into one `isAdmin()` on autopilot would silently flip that call site's polarity and widen/narrow the other two. This is the part of the refactor that needs a human decision, not a mechanical one.

## Proposed refactor

Three independent consolidations. Do them as separate commits — the sanitiser one is mechanical, the policy one is a behaviour decision.

### 1. `src/sanitize.ts` (new) — collapse three into one

```ts
export interface SanitizeOptions {
  /** Truncate to this many characters. Default 1000. */
  maxLength?: number;
  /** Reject if more than this many runs of 3+ `!`/`?`. Default 5. */
  maxPunctuationRuns?: number;
  /** Fold to lowercase above this uppercase ratio. Default 0.9. */
  shoutingRatio?: number;
  /** ...but only for strings at least this long. Default 30. */
  shoutingMinLength?: number;
}

export const SANITIZE_DEFAULTS: Required<SanitizeOptions>;

/** Returns "" for input judged unusable; otherwise the normalised string. */
export function sanitize(input: string, options?: SanitizeOptions): string;
```

One required positional arg, everything else optional and defaulted, so all three existing call shapes become `sanitize(x)`. The four magic numbers become named options rather than staying buried — that's the only added surface, and it's what makes the single implementation defensible when the next caller wants a 500-char cap.

Deliberately **not** in the API: a `role` parameter. None of the three bodies ever consulted the admin guard; the guards were separate exports sitting in the same files. Keep authorisation out of string normalisation.

### 2. `src/policy.ts` — centralise the role literals

```ts
export function isAdmin(role: string): boolean;
export function isAdminOrOwner(role: string): boolean;

// capability names stay the public surface; they delegate
export function canEditBilling(role: string): boolean;   // isAdmin
export function canSeeAuditLog(role: string): boolean;   // isAdmin
export function canImpersonate(role: string): boolean;   // isAdmin
```

`assertAdminA` → drop, replaced by `isAdmin`. `assertAdminB` → `isAdminOrOwner`. `assertAdminC` → **do not** map to `isAdmin`; either delete it or express it at the call site as `!isAdmin(role)` so the inversion is visible in the reading order. The capability functions stay because `canEditBilling` is the name worth having at a call site — the win is that `"admin"` now appears exactly once in the repo.

### 3. `src/telemetry.ts` (new) — one copy, injected clock

```ts
export interface TelemetryDeps {
  now?: () => number;                  // default Date.now
  emit?: (line: string) => void;       // default console.log
}

export function recordSanitiseEvent(
  originalLength: number,
  sanitisedLength: number,
  deps?: TelemetryDeps,
): void;
```

Optional third arg keeps both existing call shapes working and closes crimes_00004/00005 (`direct_date`) at the same time — worth folding in, since you're rewriting the function anyway and the alternative is touching it twice.

## Files that would change

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/sanitize.ts` | **new** — the single `sanitize()` implementation |
| `src/policy.ts` | modified — add `isAdmin`/`isAdminOrOwner`, delegate the three capability fns |
| `src/telemetry.ts` | **new** — single `recordSanitiseEvent` with injected clock |
| `src/sanitize-a.ts` | **deleted** |
| `src/sanitize-b.ts` | **deleted** |
| `src/sanitize-c.ts` | **deleted** |
| `src/telemetry-a.ts` | **deleted** |
| `src/telemetry-b.ts` | **deleted** |

Outright deletion is safe *here* specifically: every finding reports `blast_radius_direct_importers: 0`, and nothing in the repo imports these modules. In a codebase with real consumers, the same refactor would instead leave each old file as a deprecated one-line re-export (`export const sanitizeText = sanitize`) and delete them a release later.

## Two things to fix while you're in there

- **`replace(/[ -]/g, "")`** strips the ASCII range `0x20`–`0x2D` — space, `!"#$%&'()*+,-`. That looks like a mangled control-character strip (`[\x00-\x1F]`) rather than an intentional rule; it's silently deleting apostrophes and commas from every string. All three copies share it, so consolidating preserves the bug unless you decide otherwise. Decide before you extract, not after.
- **`if (raw === null || raw === undefined)`** is unreachable under the declared `string` type. Either widen the parameter to `string | null | undefined` (honest about what callers actually pass) or drop the guard. Don't carry the contradiction into the shared helper.

## Expected scan delta

All five findings should clear: crime_00001 and crime_00002 by construction, crime_00003 once `"admin"` has one home, and crime_00004/00005 via the injected clock. Worth re-running `crimes scan --format json` after each of the three commits rather than at the end — if the count doesn't drop the way you expect, the extraction missed a copy.

I haven't edited anything — this fixture is scanner input for the eval suite, so changing it would move the baseline. Say the word if you want the refactor applied somewhere other than `evals/fixtures/`.
